response.query: Which survey design features (incentives, attention checks, randomized framing, within-subject validation) and revealed-behavior proxies most effectively detect and correct strategic misreporting?
response.answer: Attention checks and randomized framing are effective in detecting strategic misreporting. Within-subject validation and revealed-behavior proxies also help correct such issues. These methods ensure data integrity and accuracy.

results.title: How People Use Statistics | The Review of Economic Studies
results.content: Pedro Bordalo, John Conlon, Nicola Gennaioli, Spencer Kwon, Andrei Shleifer, How People Use Statistics, *The Review of Economic Studies*, Volume 93, Issue 1, January 2026, Pages 250–285,  A large body of work formalizes specific biases such as the GF (Rabin, 2002), sample size neglect in i.i.d. draws (Benjamin *et al*., 2016), base-rate neglect (Grether, 1980), and underreaction in inference (Enke and Graeber, 2023), but does not connect biases across problems or even within different versions of the same problem.1 Second, a feature can be prominent based on the description of the problem, drawing attention because it is highly visibly displayed, as in Chetty *et al*.'s (2009) study of sales taxes. In practice, this choice does not affect our main results, as by far the most common such attention profile (28% of participants) involves paying attention to both the signal and the match feature (recall that attending to either feature in our model would yield the same answer to the inference problem).
